workload: Two 900 by 24 trajectory blocks with per-coordinate Gaussian bandwidths, as in a kernel Gram chunk.
notes: apply materializes (x_i - y_j) * scale as an (n_frames, n_frames, n_features) array and then squares it, about 300 MB for this block. The same Gram matrix is a scaled squared-distance product, which only needs the frame-by-frame result plus the scaled frames.

workload: Expectation sensitivity of one observable on a dense 100-state row-stochastic transition matrix.
notes: The body calls stationary_distribution_sensitivity once per state. Each call rechecks connectivity, refactorizes the transition matrix, and solves a least-squares problem whose matrix does not depend on the state index. One factorization and one multi-right-hand-side solve give the same linear combination with the observable.

workload: Inner-simplex representative search on the first 10 eigenvectors of a 6000-state discretization.
notes: Representative selection walks every state in Python for each cluster, with a dot and a norm per row. Each cluster step is one rank-one update of the eigenvector matrix plus a vector of norms, so the Python loop dominates on a fine discretization.

workload: Gather the frames of one hidden state across 2000 trajectories of length 500.
notes: Each trajectory is copied onto the accumulator with np.append, so the copy traffic grows with the square of the number of trajectories. One slice per trajectory and a single concatenate is linear. Bayesian HMM emission updates call this once per hidden state per Gibbs sample.
